title: Tenant-aware SLO decomposition and regional evacuation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a tenant-aware SLI/SLO decomposition approach and an operational playbook for multi-region evacuation, circuit breakers, and controlled load shedding for mixed-priority endpoints (hosted API + dedicated). The goal is to enable per-variant/per-tenant error budget accounting, automated evacuation thresholds, and graceful degradation behaviors that preserve high-priority tenants while maximizing overall availability and cost efficiency.

Background:
Current SLO work is per-endpoint and per-model oriented but lacks explicit tenant weighting and automated regional evacuation procedures. During previous surge incidents we relied on coarse circuit breakers and manual intervention, which caused unpredictable outcomes for high-value customers. We need an operational policy that: (1) decomposes endpoint-level SLOs into tenant-aware allocations, (2) provides borrowing/lending semantics for error budgets, (3) defines regional evacuation thresholds and phased failover actions, and (4) standardizes circuit breaker and load-shedding profiles per priority class.

Goals:
- Produce a clear SLI definition matrix for generation/chat/embedding endpoints by variant (vX quantized/FP16) and tenant priority (P0: enterprise-SLA, P1: paid, P2: freemium, P3: internal).
- Define error-budget accounting that supports short-term borrowing, long-term reconciliation, and automated reclamation.
- Specify multi-region evacuation policy: thresholds, windowing, pre-warm and routing rules, and rollback criteria.
- Author concrete circuit breaker and load-shedding profiles (latency percentiles, error-rate thresholds, queue-depth limits) and the mapping to graceful degradation modes (full model, response truncation, cached fallback, canned-response).
- Produce dashboards, alerts, and a runbook for on-call and SRE to operate and test policies.

Deliverables:
- Tenant SLI/SLO matrix CSV (per route, per variant, per tenant-class) and canonical examples.
- Error budget policy doc with equations for allocation, borrowing, and reclamation.
- Regional evacuation playbook (step-by-step automated/controlled stages).
- Circuit breaker and load-shedding YAML profiles for runtime configuration.
- Observability dashboard spec (Grafana + traces + logs) and alerting thresholds.
- Test harness + chaos scenarios in staging replicating cross-region capacity loss.

Proposed SLI / SLO model (high level):
- Availability SLI: fraction of successful model responses (200-level semantic success) measured over 1h and 30d windows. Success defined as requests not hitting a hard failure or deterministic fallback.
- Latency SLI: P95 over 1h for user-visible endpoints; P99 for enterprise tiers. We'll keep a separate P50/P90 set for internal regression analysis.
- Quality SLI: weighted n-gram/embedding similarity degradation checks for a small set of golden prompts run every 10m. Apply this only for model-variant level SLOs.
- Error budget allocation: endpoint-level error budget is split across tenants by normalized consumption weight (baseline tokens * tenant_priority_multiplier). Default multiplier mapping: P0=4, P1=2, P2=1, P3=0.25 (strings).

Error budget borrowing and reclamation policy:
- Borrowing: A tenant can borrow up to 20% of another lower-priority tenant pool for windows up to 6 hours if the donor tenant is underutilizing their allocation. Borrow actions are recorded and backfilled in the budget ledger.
- Reconciliation: If a tenant borrows, their future allocation is reduced on a linear schedule over the next 30 days until repaid. Emergency admin override allowed for one-off remediation.
- Automated reclamation: When global capacity drops (regional outage), we demote borrowing and reclaim lower-priority budgets immediately for redistribution to enterprise tenants.

Regional evacuation and failover policy (phased):
- Phase 0 (pre-failure): Continuous regional health scoring (capacity headroom, queue depth, GPU utilization, tail latency). If regional score < 0.7 for 5m, move to Phase 1.
- Phase 1 (protect): Limit acceptance of P2/P3 traffic into region; enable cached and partial responses for P2/P3. If score < 0.5 for 3m, proceed to Phase 2.
- Phase 2 (evacuate non-critical): Gradually shift P1 traffic to alternate region(s) using weighted routing over 2m windows, with concurrent spin-up of model-variants in target regions. P0 traffic is routed preferentially to healthy regions.
- Phase 3 (full regional failover): Redirect all traffic according to priority-preserving policies and enable per-tenant circuit-breaker overrides. Post-mortem window begins after stabilization.

Circuit breaker and load-shedding profiles:
- Circuit-breaker buckets by priority class: thresholds defined in YAML deliverable. Example (P0): error-rate 1% over 5m OR P99 latency > 2s => short-circuit to warm fallback variant; (P1): error-rate 2.5% OR P99 > 3s => degrade to partial response; (P2/P3): stricter shedding e.g., queue-limit 500 per model-shard, drop new requests beyond limit.
- Load-shedding strategies: token-budget-based admission, prefix-KV cache first, response-length truncation, cached-answer fallback, synthetic honeypot for abusive traffic.

Observability and enforcement:
- Dashboards: 1) SLO overview with per-tenant burn rates; 2) regional health map; 3) circuit-breaker events table; 4) error-budget ledger.
- Alerts: automated page for P0 burn rate > 10% in 15m; paging for any unexpected region evacuation trigger.
- Enforcement: runtime reads YAML profiles; policy service exposes a read-only endpoint for Console and an admin endpoint for overrides. Auditing required (audit event per override).

Testing & rollout:
- Validate in staging with chaos monkey scenarios: single-region GPU isolation, network partition, and burst from synthetic tenants.
- Canary rollout: enable tenant-weighting for 5% of tenants (preferably opt-in enterprise lab) for two weeks. Collect burn-rate and false-positive rate metrics.
- Release plan: feature-flagged rollout, release notes, and a training session for SRE/Support.

Acceptance criteria:
- Completed SLI/SLO matrix and error-budget doc reviewed by PM, SRE, and Product (sign-offs captured).
- Playbook implements phased evacuation steps and can be executed end-to-end in staging with automated indicators.
- Circuit-breaker profiles deployed behind feature flag and verified with load tests.
- Dashboards and alerts are operational with synthetic tests exercising burn-rate alerts.

Notes/limitations:
- This work scopes behavioral policy and tooling. Kernel/runtime-level autoscaling optimizations and model-level quantization recommendations will be separate tickets (see dependencies).
- Quality SLI instrumentation for new models requires per-model golden prompts; we'll coordinate with Applied ML.
